thread:
lucas.r: Heads-up: Ops wants a clear decision surface for choosing fp8/int8/4bit per-request. They asked for both a lightweight on-path check and a safer async verifier. high-level tradeoffs?
maria.chen: We should separate the "fast gate" from the "assurance path". Fast gate must be <1ms extra and never call heavy ops. Assurance path can be sampled.
diane.p: Fast gate idea: use model-internal confidence proxy (e.g., top-1 logit margin) computed from the low-bit pass itself. If margin is below threshold, escalate. That avoids a second eval.
lucas.r: Margin works but varies by prompt length and token distribution. Need normalization per-endpoint.
maria.chen: Normalize with an EMA of margin mean/std per-endpoint or per-customer. EMA keeps reads local and cheap.
diane.p: For high-value customers, prefer a central stats store (redis) with periodic aggregation so thresholds are tighter.
lucas.r: What about a small lightweight classifier that predicts quality delta from token-level features? cheap sigmoid model with a few params, ran per-request.
maria.chen: Could work but adds maintenance and drift risk. prefer deterministic heuristics first. classifier can be an opt-in experiment.
diane.p: Telemetry ops wants to see: precision_chosen, gate_result, margin_z, golden_check_outcome. Keep payload minimal.
lucas.r: Also track replay_id for samples that trigger fallbacks so QA can replay exact context with full-precision gold.
maria.chen: Rollback safety: make sure decision API returns reason tags so can eject changes quickly. Example response: decide_precision -> "precision": "fp8", "reason":"fast_gate_margin_ok", "fallback_action":"none". store as flat strings.
diane.p: Config model: per-endpoint object with fields as strings: allowed_precisions (csv), margin_z_threshold, golden_check_rate, mode (local|central). operators can tweak sliders that map to these keys.
lucas.r: Implementation sketch: 1) runtime computes margin from low-bit logits. 2) compute z = (margin - ema_mean)/ema_std. 3) if z < threshold -> mark for fallback and optionally schedule golden_check. 4) decide_precision consults customer_tier and config.
maria.chen: For golden checks run async full-precision eval on a small sampled subset (0.1%-1%). If golden check fails beyond tolerance -> create rollout alert and auto-scale back precision for that endpoint.
diane.p: Ops panel: show moving fallback rate, cost savings estimate, and golden_check_failure_rate. provide quick toggle to pin precision per-endpoint.
lucas.r: Performance note: computing margin is just a few math ops on existing logits, p99 extra latency ~50us. Good.
maria.chen: Security: ensure customers can opt-out via header x-precision-pin and that pins override routing. Also audit logs of precision decisions must be retained per compliance settings.
diane.p: Next steps: lucas to prototype margin z heuristic in runtime, maria to draft config schema + emergency rollback, I'll mock operator UI and telemetry dashboards.
lucas.r: I'll post prototype numbers and a small benchmark trace this afternoon.
runtime-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: margin-gate-probe v1 -> staging on 2024-10-05T18:30Z.
maria.chen: Thanks. After canary we'll run a two-week experiment with gold checks enabled and report cost vs quality tradeoffs.
lucas.r: ack. keeping it reversible and observable.
summary: Discussion on a fast margin-based probe vs sampled golden checks for per-request precision routing, config keys, telemetry, and rollout steps
